text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 1.47% today, extending a two-week climb of 3.79%. The gain reflects heightened geopolitical tension in the Middle East—specifically, a U.S. Navy blockade of Iran that is sharply reducing Iran's oil exports. When a major oil producer loses export capacity, global oil supplies tighten, which typically supports refining margins and boosts demand for U.S. refiners like Marathon, especially one running at near-peak capacity (97.4% utilization).

The stock's steady climb over the past week aligns with escalating Iran sanctions news, which has accumulated as the Trump administration intensified economic pressure through the blockade. Refinery margins improve when crude supply becomes constrained while domestic fuel demand remains steady—and with U.S. refineries already running hot and fuel inventories relatively modest, the blockade creates the conditions refiners profit from.
